name: des_process
description: A discrete event simulation of a queue or process network, run and drawn: sources → stations (a lane of waiting tokens before c server boxes, busy or idle) → delays → sinks (with a counter), routes with their shares, the entities as tokens where the simulation has them at time t, a readout per station (waiting, % busy, mean wait), a clock, and a chart: queue length over time with a cursor at t, or mean wait against utilisation with queueing theory's curve. Choose it for ANY question about queues, waiting lines, servers, utilisation, bottlenecks, patient flow, Little's law, M/M/1, M/M/c, or simulating a process. `t` ANIMATES — set t: 0, then {"animate": {"t": 120}, "duration": 8} runs the simulation on screen (tokens flow); animating a rate or service time ("nodes.0.rate") re-runs it (hold t at the horizon to watch the queue grow). The same seed is the same run. Paused, the viewer drags the clock or the chart's cursor, scrubs or types a rate, a service time, a CV or a share, taps ⊖ ⊕ for servers and "new run" for another seed; an explore beat naming nothing invites this. Numbers for text: {des.t}, {des.arrivals}, {des.departures}, {des.in_system}, {des.L}, {des.W}, {des.lambda}; per station {des.<id>_queue}, _busy, _servers, _util (%), _wait, _avg_queue, _throughput, _served, _balked, _rho (fraction) and for M/M/c or M/G/1 _wq_theory, _lq_theory; the first station's also without the prefix ({des.util}, {des.wait}, {des.rho}, {des.wq_theory}); {des.<sink>_done}.
interaction: Scrub time on the clock or a chart; scrub arrival rates, service times, CVs and branch shares; tap plus or minus for a server more or fewer, 'new run' for another seed.

label.description: A word or two on the canvas (default: the id; a source's is the entity's plural, a sink's "done").

rate.description: source: arrivals per time unit (random, Poisson).

every.description: source: instead, one arrival every this many time units.

interarrival.description: source: instead, the gap between arrivals, as service.

variability.description: Advanced. The gaps' (source) or times' (station, delay) coefficient of variation, mean kept: 0 regular, 1 random (the default), 2 bursty. Draws a scrubbable "CV 1.0"; animate nodes.<i>.variability.

schedule.description: Advanced. source, instead of rate: {times: [0, 120, 240], rates: [0.1, 0.3, 0.2]}, each rate from its time on (shape: "smooth" joins them); drawn in the first time chart.

batch.description: Advanced. source: groups of this size arrive together, or {mean} (geometric); rate still counts entities.

priority.description: source: its entities' class, 1 = most urgent (coloured apart).

service.description: station: time to serve one. A number = random (exponential) with that mean; or {dist: "fixed", value} | {dist: "uniform", min, max} | {dist: "triangular", min, mode, max} | {dist: "lognormal", mean, sd} | {dist: "gamma", mean, cv} | {dist: "exponential", mean}.

time.description: delay: time spent there (no queue), as service.

capacity.description: station: the most that may wait; more are turned away.

discipline.description: station: priority serves the lowest class first.

to.description: Where entities go next: an id, or shares {"xray": 0.3, "doctor": 0.7} summing to 1. Default: the next node in the list.

nodes.description: The network, left to right: at least a source, a station and a sink.

horizon.description: Length of the run (default 120). Keep arrivals under ~3000.

t.description: The time shown (default: the horizon). Animate it to run the simulation.

chart.description: "queue" (default: waiting at the first station over time), "wait" (each wait and the running mean), "system" (number in the system), "wait_util" (mean wait against % busy, theory curve and the run's dot), an object {of, station, y_max}, a list of two (side by side), or false.

readouts.description: The readout under each station (default true).

controls.description: The ⊖ ⊕ server buttons and "new run" (default true).

transit.description: Time units a token takes along an arrow on screen (default: short — horizon/120 at most).

element_ids.node_<id>: a source's or sink's ring (a sink's with its counter), a delay's box with its tokens; for a station, the SET of all its parts
element_ids.queue_<id>: a station's lane with its waiting tokens (and a "+n" when more wait than fit)
element_ids.server_<id>: a station's server boxes, shaded when busy, a token in each
element_ids.label_<id> / rate_<id> / service_<id>: a node's name; a source's arrival rate; a station's or delay's time
element_ids.var_<id> / schedule_<id>: a node's "CV 1.0"; a scheduled source's rate band in the first time chart, a dot at t
element_ids.readout_<id>: a station's readout: waiting, % busy, mean wait
element_ids.route_<a>_<b> / share_<a>_<b>: the arrow from a to b with the tokens travelling it; its share ("30%") on a branch
element_ids.nodes / routes: SETS — every node part; every arrow and share
element_ids.chart: SET — the chart: axes, x_ticks, y_ticks, x_label, y_label, chart_line (the quantity up to t), cursor (at t), warmup (shaded); a "wait" chart adds chart_dots; "wait_util" has theory_curve, theory_dot, sim_dot. A second chart's ids end _2 (chart_2).
element_ids.title: the title, when set

examples.request: Why do customers queue at a single checkout even when the cashier is not always busy?
Simulate patient flow in an emergency department: triage, then some need an X-ray before they see a doctor.
Why does the emergency waiting room overflow around midday when triage copes on average?
